benchmark.name: TALENT
benchmark.description: TALENT (Tabular Analytics and LEarNing Toolbox) is a large-scale tabular benchmark and toolbox from the LAMDA group at Nanjing University. Its basic benchmark has 300 real-world datasets, each with one fixed 64%/16%/20% train/validation/test split; the official protocol runs every method in its default (or tuned) configuration with 15 random seeds, scores classification by accuracy and regression by RMSE, and aggregates by average rank across datasets. The toolbox implements 40+ classical and deep tabular methods and (as of 2025-26) wrappers for TabPFN v1/v2/v2.5/v3, Real-TabPFN, TabICL/TabICLv2, Mitra, LimiX, TabDPT and TabFM. Benchmark paper: 'A Closer Look at Deep Learning Methods on Tabular Datasets' (arXiv 2407.00956, v4 Nov 2025); toolbox paper: 'TALENT: A Tabular Analytics and Learning Toolbox' (arXiv 2407.04057).
benchmark.task_breakdown: 300 basic datasets: 120 binary classification, 80 multiclass classification (12 of them with more than 10 classes), 100 regression. Extensions: a 'large' benchmark (22 datasets) and later large-data / high-dimensional TALENT-extension datasets (the TabPFN-3.5 report evaluates 337 datasets with <= 1M training rows including extensions). Common subsets used by TFM papers: 274 = 300 minus the 26 TabPFN-2/TabICLv2 development datasets ('TabICLv2 protocol'; 173 cls <= 10 classes, 12 cls > 10 classes, 89 regression); 288 = 300 minus the 12 datasets with > 10 classes; 188 classification = 200 minus those 12.
benchmark.official_leaderboard: https://6sy666.github.io/TALENT-Results/ (also results/cls_bin.md, results/cls_multi.md, results/regression.md in the repo): per-dataset mean accuracy / RMSE over 15 seeds for 31 classical and deep methods; TabPFN v1 is the only foundation model included. The README's Performance-Efficiency-Size figure (dated 2025-10-05) additionally shows TabPFN v2 (figure only, no printed numbers). No official TALENT table lists any of the 2026 tabular foundation models compared here (checked 2026-09-23).
benchmark.notes: There is no official TALENT leaderboard for tabular foundation models; all numbers below are self-reported evaluations from model papers, each with its own dataset subset, context policy, comparison pool and metric, so tables from different sources must not be merged or compared directly. Elo values in particular are relative to each source's own pool (Random Forest anchored at 1000 in Mitra-v2 and LimiX-2). The TabPFN-3 report (arXiv 2605.13986) evaluates TabPFN-3 on the 274-dataset TabICLv2 protocol and per task type (Figures 13, 28), on the 4 many-class (100-class) datasets (Figure 29) and on 14 large-row (100k-1M) datasets (Figure 30), and states TabPFN-3 ranks first in each view, but prints no numbers (bar charts only); TabPFN-3's printed rank on that protocol (4.48) comes from the TabPFN-3.5 report, where TabPFN-3.5 was added to the pool. The Causilo technical report (arXiv 2609.22866) and the TabPFN-2.5 / RealTabPFN-2.5 report (arXiv 2511.08667, v2) contain no TALENT evaluation; TabFM (Google Research) has no paper or technical report and its GitHub repo publishes only TabArena result files, so all TabFM TALENT numbers come from third-party reports (EXAONE, Xiaomi-TabLDM, Mitra-v2, LimiX-2). TabPFN-3.5-Fast and Causilo have no TALENT numbers in any source; TabPFN-2.6 appears only in the Xiaomi-TabLDM report. Added 2026-09-30: NVIDIA Kumo Tabular's TALENT ranks are self-reported in its release blog only.

tables.source_title: TabICLv2: A better, faster, scalable, and open tabular foundation model (arXiv 2602.11139, v2 16 Sep 2026; v1 Feb 2026)
tables.protocol: TabICLv2 paper, Appendix K (numbers as printed in the text; the full comparisons are critical-difference diagrams, i.e. figures). TALENT base benchmark (300 datasets: 120 binary, 80 multiclass, 100 regression), fixed 64%/16%/20% train/validation/test split per dataset, minus the datasets used for TabICLv2 development ('for a fair comparison, we exclude the development datasets'; the TabPFN-3 and TabPFN-3.5 reports and the Mitra-v2 report, which reuse this protocol, document it as 300 - 26 = 274 datasets). Metric: average rank across datasets (lower is better) based on accuracy for classification and RMSE for regression unless stated otherwise. All models at default hyperparameters (no per-dataset tuning); 32 estimators for TabICLv2 and for TabPFN-2.5/RealTabPFN-2.5 on TALENT; TabICL uses the TabICLv1.1 checkpoint. Number of seeds not stated in the paper (TALENT's default is 15).
tables.notes: Appendix K.2 'Results on all datasets'. Pairwise win rates of TabICLv2: 62% vs RealTabPFN-2.5, 65% vs TabPFN-2.5 (binomial test p=0.0018 on accuracy for TabICLv2 vs RealTabPFN-2.5, Table L.2). The CD diagram (Figure K.1) also contains TabICL, CatBoost, XGBoost and the other TALENT baselines, but their ranks are only in the figure and are omitted here. Main-text B.1 (Figure B.1, a different comparison pool that adds the TabICLv2 Stage-1/Stage-2 checkpoints) gives TabICLv2 (final Stage 3) an all-datasets average rank of 5.41 (Stage 1: 9.94, Stage 2: 5.69).

tables.source_title: Mitra-v2 Technical Report (arXiv 2609.04540v1, 3 Sep 2026)
tables.protocol: Mitra-v2 report, Section 4 (TALENT boards). Preset main274 = TALENT 300 minus the 26 TabPFN-2/TabICLv2 development datasets (15 classification, 11 regression), i.e. 274 datasets: 173 classification with <= 10 classes (accuracy), 12 classification with > 10 classes (accuracy), 89 regression (RMSE); slices are never mixed except in the joint board. One fixed 64/16/20 split per dataset, 15 seeds (0-14) per method, no time limit, every method at its author-recommended default configuration (Mitra-v2 in its default deployment configuration: fine-tuned per its standard recipe with eight-fold bagging; > 10-class tasks via its hierarchical decomposition). Comparison pool: native TALENT baselines (boosted trees, RealMLP, ModernNCA, TabR, FT-Transformer, ...) plus TabPFN-3, TabICLv2, TabFM, EXAONE Tabular and Mitra-v2. Elo = Bradley-Terry fit over per-dataset pairwise comparisons, anchored at RandomForest = 1,000, 95% intervals from a 2,000-round bootstrap; rank = average rank. Rare failed cells imputed (KNN-5 within slice for classification, median for regression) and disclosed per method. Context policy of this table: TRAIN-ONLY (every in-context model uses the train split alone as its support set; TabFM and EXAONE Tabular were re-run accordingly over the same 15 seeds). This is the report's headline board (Figure 1).
tables.notes: Table 7, joint main274 board, train-only context (headline). 95% intervals: TabFM +62/-56, Mitra-v2 +60/-54, EXAONE +52/-46, TabPFN-3 +54/-50, TabICLv2 +54/-49, ModernNCA +43/-42, RealMLP +45/-43, CatBoost +30/-29, LightGBM +29/-29, XGBoost +27/-25. The top three (TabFM, Mitra-v2, EXAONE) are statistically indistinguishable. Table 7 lists the top 12 of the pool by Elo; the two rows not in this comparison's model list are TabR (train-only Elo 1,142.6 / rank 12.22; train+val 1,143.3 / 12.25) and FT-Transformer (1,062.2 / 14.81; 1,062.4 / 14.84). Imputed cells out of 274 (train-only / train+val): TabFM 13 / 12, EXAONE 1 / 0, TabPFN-3 1 / 1, TabICLv2 1 / 1, ModernNCA 6 / 6, Mitra-v2 0 / 0, others 0 / 0.

per_model_summary.limix-2: LimiX-2 reports the top TALENT Elo in its own evaluation (LimiX-2 report, 288 datasets, 15 seeds): overall 1506 vs 1471 for TabFM, with the best Elo on classification (1475), regression (1584), binary (1455) and multiclass (1520), the lowest improvability (6.75%), the highest aggregated win count (84.3) and the lowest average rank in every task type (4.62 / 3.91 / 3.88). No other source evaluates LimiX-2 on TALENT.
per_model_summary.tabpfn-3.5: TabPFN-3.5 ranks first on TALENT in its own report: average rank 2.95 on the 274-dataset TabICLv2 protocol (TabPFN-3 4.48, TabICLv2 5.35) and 2.13 on all 337 datasets with <= 1M training rows incl. extensions (TabPFN-3 3.20; '1 of 37', 80% per-dataset win rate vs TabICLv2, 91% vs CatBoost). Not included in the LimiX-2, Mitra-v2, Xiaomi or EXAONE TALENT tables (all published before or around the same time).
per_model_summary.tabpfn-3.5-fast: Not evaluated on TALENT: the TabPFN-3.5 report states that on TALENT only TabPFN-3.5 itself was evaluated ('no other family member was evaluated'). No numbers in any source.
per_model_summary.causilo: No TALENT results: the Causilo technical report evaluates TabArena, BeyondArena and ScoringBench only, and Causilo does not appear in any other paper's TALENT table (LimiX-2 mentions Causilo only on TabArena).
per_model_summary.tabfm: TabFM (Google Research; no paper) is evaluated on TALENT only by third parties, where it is consistently in the leading group: best mean accuracy on 188 classification datasets (0.863) and second mean R^2 on regression (0.733) in the EXAONE report; best overall (4.23) and regression (3.72) average rank in the Xiaomi-TabLDM report; top Elo on the Mitra-v2 main274 boards (1,503.2 train-only / 1,527.7 train+val, statistically tied with Mitra-v2 and EXAONE); runner-up Elo 1471 in the LimiX-2 report. It cannot run the 12 > 10-class datasets.
per_model_summary.mitra-v2: Mitra-v2's own report (274 datasets, 15 seeds, Elo anchored at RandomForest = 1000) places it in the leading group with TabFM and EXAONE Tabular: Elo 1,479.7 (avg rank 4.39) with train-only context and 1,490.2 (4.35) with train+val context, first outright on the 12 many-class datasets (Elo 2,070.1 / 2,204.2) and highest train-only regression Elo (1,499.3). In the LimiX-2 report's pool it is much lower (overall Elo 1269, 9th of 19).
per_model_summary.exaone-tabular: EXAONE Tabular reports second-best mean accuracy on 188 TALENT classification datasets (0.857, vs 0.863 for TabFM) and the best mean R^2 on 100 regression datasets (0.736) in its own report (support set capped at 50k rows). Third parties: Mitra-v2 report Elo 1,451.8 train-only / 1,519.0 train+val (avg rank 4.83 / 3.94; statistically tied with TabFM and Mitra-v2), Xiaomi report avg rank 4.96 overall / 4.15 regression / 6.38 binary, LimiX-2 report overall Elo 1393 (4th, behind LimiX-2, TabFM and AutoGluon).
per_model_summary.tabpfn-3: The TabPFN-3 report says TabPFN-3 ranks first on TALENT (274-dataset TabICLv2 protocol, per task type, many-class and large-row slices) but prints no numbers. Printed numbers from other sources: avg rank 4.48 (274 datasets, TabPFN-3.5 report, behind TabPFN-3.5's 2.95) and 3.20 (337 datasets); mean accuracy 0.854 / mean R^2 0.728 (EXAONE report); avg rank 5.55 overall / 4.88 regression / 6.80 binary (Xiaomi report); Elo 1,414.8 train-only (rank 5.48) in the Mitra-v2 report; Elo 1363 in the LimiX-2 report.
per_model_summary.xiaomi-tabldm: Xiaomi-TabLDM's report (TabICLv2 protocol, KNN-imputed missing cells) gives it average rank 4.82 overall (2nd behind TabFM 4.23), 4.03 on 100 regression datasets (2nd behind TabFM 3.72) and 5.72 on binary classification (tied best with TabFM). In the LimiX-2 report it has overall Elo 1341 (7th of 19).
per_model_summary.tabpfn-2.6: Only the Xiaomi-TabLDM report includes TabPFN-2.6 on TALENT: average rank 6.79 overall and 6.33 on regression (last among the six named foundation models in that comparison). No other source reports it.
per_model_summary.realtabpfn-2.5: The TabPFN-2.5 / RealTabPFN-2.5 report itself contains no TALENT evaluation. In the TabICLv2 paper (274 datasets, 32 estimators) RealTabPFN-2.5 has average rank 5.11 overall (vs TabICLv2 4.66 and TabPFN-2.5 5.45), 4.82 on binary accuracy (best), 5.64 on multiclass accuracy, and is beaten by TabICLv2 on AUC/log-loss ranks; it also appears as a baseline bar in the TabPFN-3 / TabPFN-3.5 TALENT figures (no printed numbers).
per_model_summary.tabiclv2: TabICLv2's own paper reports the best average rank on TALENT (4.66 vs RealTabPFN-2.5 5.11, TabPFN-2.5 5.45, LimiX 8.34, TabPFNv2 8.82; 62% win rate vs RealTabPFN-2.5). Later third-party reports place it below the newest models: 5.35 (TabPFN-3.5 report, 274 datasets), 6.15 overall / 6.10 regression / 6.90 binary (Xiaomi report), Elo 1,399.6 (rank 5.76) train-only in the Mitra-v2 report, mean accuracy 0.854 / R^2 0.723 (EXAONE report), Elo 1344 (LimiX-2 report).
per_model_summary.tabicl: TabICL (v1.1 checkpoint) appears only in the TabICLv2 paper's binary-classification ranks (8.48 vs TabICLv2 4.98).
per_model_summary.tabpfn-2.5: TabPFN-2.5 (no real-data fine-tuning) appears in the TabICLv2 paper: average rank 5.45 overall, 5.28 binary accuracy, 4.43 regression MAE rank (better than TabICLv2's 4.63).
per_model_summary.tabpfnv2: TabPFNv2 appears in the TabICLv2 paper with overall average rank 8.82; it is also the only v2-generation foundation model in TALENT's own README figure (no printed number).
per_model_summary.limix: LimiX v1 appears in the TabICLv2 paper (avg rank 8.34 overall, 8.61 binary), the EXAONE report (mean accuracy 0.834, mean R^2 0.713) and, as LimiX-16M, in the LimiX-2 report (overall Elo 1227).
per_model_summary.mitra: Mitra v1 has no TALENT number in any of the sources (the Mitra-v2 report omits Mitra-v1 Elo values by design).
per_model_summary.tabdpt: TabDPT appears in the EXAONE report (mean accuracy 0.849, mean R^2 0.715) and the LimiX-2 report (overall Elo 1272).
per_model_summary.catboost: CatBoost: Mitra-v2 report Elo 1,153.2 (rank 11.89) train-only main274 and 1,155.4 (11.80) full300; LimiX-2 report overall Elo 1094 (best tree/neural baseline there); TabPFN-3.5 wins 91% of 337 datasets against it.
per_model_summary.xgboost: XGBoost: Mitra-v2 report Elo 1,091.9 (rank 13.83); LimiX-2 report overall Elo 999; rank 14.60 on TALENT datasets > 10K samples in the TabICLv2 paper's stage ablation.
per_model_summary.lightgbm: LightGBM: Mitra-v2 report Elo 1,115.9 (rank 13.06); LimiX-2 report overall Elo 973.
per_model_summary.realmlp: RealMLP: Mitra-v2 report Elo 1,166.1 (rank 11.50); LimiX-2 report overall Elo 1069.
per_model_summary.tabm: TabM: LimiX-2 report overall Elo 953 (lowest of the listed methods there); not in the other TALENT tables.
per_model_summary.modernnca: ModernNCA: Mitra-v2 report Elo 1,166.9 (rank 11.48; best classical baseline there); LimiX-2 report overall Elo 1055.
per_model_summary.kumo-tabular: Only NVIDIA's own blog reports TALENT numbers for Kumo Tabular (2026-09-29): 'top overall ranking' on the corrected 300-dataset TALENT benchmark (official pipeline, 15 seeds) with average ranks 6.67 on classification accuracy, 3.98 on classification log-loss and 4.22 on regression RMSE; the size is not stated in the text and no third-party TALENT evaluation exists yet.
